title: Materials: stress, strain and elastic response
mission: Curate atomic reusable strength-of-materials relationships: stress, strain, elastic response, safety factors and density, each with explicit geometry and loading scope. Successive batches; no structural-analysis chain required.
priorities: Normal stress from axial force and cross-sectional area
Engineering normal strain from elongation and original length
Hooke uniaxial response from elastic modulus and strain
Factor of safety from failure and allowable stress
Mass density from mass and volume
boundaries: Uniaxial, quasi-static scope must be explicit; separate stress from pressure, engineering strain from true strain, and stiffness from strength.
True strain and any logarithmic, plastic or rate-dependent forms must be deferred with sources.
Exclude fatigue, fracture mechanics, creep, buckling analysis beyond stated algebraic scope, and material selection advice.
Modulus values are supplied material parameters with sources, never universal constants.
starter_sources: No source URLs were preverified for this assignment. Find a mechanics-of-materials textbook (for example Hibbeler, or Beer and Johnston) or an agency materials reference; record exact book, edition and section. Discovery snippets alone do not prove the equation.
special_checks: Area and length units must be explicit; reject zero-area and zero-length denominators
Elastic-limit assumptions must be stated; test a zero-load boundary
Factor-of-safety records must state failure-vs-allowable ordering conventions
Bending-stress and column formulas belong to later coverage via the guidance, not forced into this batch
integration_expectation: Stress and pressure dimensions are unsupported and require extension; strain, safety-factor and density records are scalar ratios that fit the engine once meanings exist. Keep full SI units and never relabel stress as force.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
